title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models
read_level: partial (arXiv HTML v2 dated 23 Nov 2026: main text Secs 1, 3-6, Limitations, Appendix J Cost read; Sec 2 Related Work and Appendices A-I not read; figures as text only)
metadata_mismatch: none in title/authors; notes are from v2 (v1 not read)
why_wsp: Frontier LLM editors in a Python kernel read and overwrite parameters of a smaller LM (no gradients, <=50 executions) so it performs a task zero-shot that it previously did only with 16 in-context examples.
facets: application domain: LLM in-context learning / task internalisation
domain: LLM in-context learning internalised into weights (word-mapping tasks, arithmetic, compositional tasks, GSM8K prompt internalisation)
editor: Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra (highest reasoning settings); appendix: open-weight GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
target: Primary Qwen2.5-0.5B (494M, fp32); scale: Qwen2.5-1.5B, 7B, 14B; families: Llama-3.2-1B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base
interface: code/tensor tools (persistent Python kernel with model as PyTorch module)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (agentic, up to 50 model executions, 80 or 150 turns)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "modifying 0.002–0.9% of the parameters (median per editor)" (Sec 1); Table 2 medians: Fable 5.1 8,512 (0.002%), Opus 5.5 4,358,075 (0.882%), Gemini 4 374,080 (0.076%), GPT-6 Astra 545,664 (0.110%)

headline_results.quote: The editors' updates reach a mean of 88.5% (Fable 5.1) and 90.4% (Opus 5.5) against 89.3% for 16-shot ICL
With every run scored as it was left, the four editors reach 89.7%, 80.5%, 87.6% and 92.6% (Table 4), so Opus 5.5 falls below the baselines
the editors differ from these four baselines by -0.7 to +6.1 points ... None of the differences survives correction for multiple comparisons
over three splits Gemini 4 Argon reaches 85.8% and GPT-6 Astra 81.0% (baselines 86.5–88.2%)
under a question-answer wording, accuracy falls to 13% (Fable 5.1), where ICL retains 89% and the rank-1 gradient update 48%
14 of 18 runs finished within the turn limit and reach 94% on test (83% with the unfinished runs scored as they stood), against 90% for ICL
in 89 of 138 annotated runs the editor's main strategy was to inject the task vector
At 7B the 6 completed programs average 89.7%, against 73.0% for LoRA and 79.0% for a rank-1 update
none of the 44 updates below 100K parameters raises perplexity by more than 5%, 4 of 41 between 100K and 10M do, and 5 of 14 above 10M do
59.1% against 40.8% unedited, 59.0% with the step-by-step trigger appended and 67.4% with the sixteen examples in context

cost.quote: all 18 runs completed in 4–27 turns at about $1 per run, against $4–7 for the others
$156 for Fable 5.1, about $105 for Opus 5.5, and about €300 ($325) for Gemini 4 Argon ... $95.62 for GPT-6 Astra
Evaluation and baselines add approximately 13 GPU-hours in total.

baselines_and_controls: Unedited zero-shot; 16-shot ICL; scripted task vectors (gated 1/2 units, constant, implicit rank-1 after Dherin et al.); Adam all weights; LoRA (q,v); matched rank-1 FT; context distillation; gradient baselines also given editor-written pairs; random edit with matched norm/sparsity; ICL task-vector patching; strict-data (no own pairs) condition.
runs_and_variance: Three data splits (seeds) on 0.5B; mean ± s.d. per cell; scale, family and hybrid experiments single split. Quote: 'the scale experiments, the family replication, and the hybrid condition use a single split' (Limitations)
robustness_of_edits: Prompt-wording shift tested (fails: 13% under QA wording for Fable 5.1; 20.9% on five unseen wordings for wording-agnostic condition); interference on other tasks and WikiText-2 perplexity/ARC-Easy measured; no fine-tuning/quantization survival tests
verification: none formal; audit of all tool calls for leakage; separate application of 'readable' part of updates; paired tests with multiple-comparison correction
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editors bring task knowledge: 'about half of the runs type task pairs (examples) of their own, which contain up to 98% of the hidden test inputs'. When test inputs shown without labels, 'the editor memorises them wherever the task has no rule' (held-out 0-17% on antonym/capital/translation). 95 of 138 runs used the terms task vector or function vector unprompted.
limitations_stated: One main model family; single splits for scale/family; tasks where ICL already strong; editor told the evaluation template; editor task knowledge; kernel not sandboxed (audit found harness imports, filesystem searches, WikiText-2 cache loads; an open-weight editor read task definitions and was set aside); forward-pass budget circumvented by Gemini via CPU reimplementation; LLM-annotated strategies not human-validated; closed-form context compilers not compared.
cites_or_builds_on: Hendel et al. 2023 and Todd et al. 2024 (task/function vectors)
notes_for_survey: Controlled comparison of four frontier editors against ICL, LoRA, full fine-tuning and context distillation on the same 16 examples. Reports unfinished-run accounting, editor prior knowledge as a confound, and a non-sandboxed kernel with audited leakage. Authors' conclusion: 'weight-space programming adds legibility, not accuracy.'
